title: unified-rollouts: canary + A/B + shadow autorollback enhancements
author: Aisha Patel
description: This PR enhances the unified rollouts engine to improve safety and observability for combined canary, A/B and shadow deployments and to make automated rollback decisions more robust. Motivations: 1) incidents where noisy telemetry caused premature rollbacks; 2) support for multi-variant A/B experiments alongside shadow probing; 3) better operational visibility for SRE and platform teams. Changes include: - rollout engine: add composite metric evaluation (weighted metrics with priority tiers), configurable metric quorums, and per-stage timeout/quarantine windows; - canary scheduling: new staged weight schedule (0->10->30->60->100) with linear smoothing and optional hold points; - A/B experiments: variant tagging and experiment isolation so A/B traffic won't trigger rollbacks for unrelated rollout paths; - shadow probing: time-windowed shadow sampling with adaptive sampling rate based on current load and recent error-rate deltas; - autorollback policy: multi-metric quorum semantics, metric debounce (short-term noise suppression), safety guards that require both absolute and relative thresholds before triggering rollback; - observability: new telemetry events (rollout.stage_transition, rollout.quarantine_entered, rollout.rollback_reason), additional tags for model_version, route_id, and experiment_id; - e2e and integration tests: added simulated traffic harnesses to exercise staged canary, A/B splits, shadow probes, and autorollback flows under noisy telemetry; - docs: rollout policy reference and runbook updates. Checklist: [x] unit tests for evaluation logic [x] integration tests for staged canary [x] e2e traffic simulation harness [x] docs and runbook updates [x] feature-flag gated rollout engine update Release note: see release_notes field. Related: ENG-1423 (design), ENG-1587 (infra follow-up), SUP-908 (customer incident). CI: initial unit failure on flaky metric aggregator was fixed by debouncing; full CI passed after two reruns. Merge: squash and merge after final approval. Notes for reviewers: pay attention to the quorum semantics (docs included) and the defaults for sampling rate and debounce window; these are conservative but can be tuned per-customer via rollout policy config.
